# dtcloud_router_interface (Resource)

Attaches a private network to a router, which is what gives the machines on that network a route to everywhere else.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_router_interface" "app" {
  router_id  = dtcloud_router.main.id
  network_id = dtcloud_network.app.id
}

# With a chosen address rather than one the platform picks. This is also the only
# path on which port_security_enabled reaches the platform.
resource "dtcloud_router_interface" "db" {
  router_id             = dtcloud_router.main.id
  network_id            = dtcloud_network.db.id
  ip_address            = "10.0.20.1"
  port_security_enabled = true
}
```

-> **Nothing here changes in place.** The platform has an attach endpoint and a detach endpoint and
nothing in between, so every argument replaces the attachment.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `network_id` (String) ID of the network to attach. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `router_id` (String) ID of the router to attach the network to. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `ip_address` (String) Address the interface takes on the network. When omitted, the platform attaches to the network's first subnet and allocates an address from it. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `port_security_enabled` (Boolean) Whether port security applies to this interface. It only reaches the platform when `ip_address` is set; attaching without one goes through a path that does not take the setting. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `cidr` (String) CIDR of the attached network's first subnet.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `network_name` (String) Name of the attached network.
- `port_id` (String) ID of the port the platform created for this interface.
- `status` (String) Status of the interface's port.
- `subnet_id` (String) ID of the subnet the interface's address came from.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **Without `ip_address` you land on the network's first subnet.** Not one you name, and not all of
  them. Networks created by `dtcloud_network` have exactly one subnet, so this only matters on a
  network built elsewhere with several.
* **`port_security_enabled` applies only when `ip_address` is set.** The two ways of attaching are
  different operations, not one operation with a field left out: asking for a specific address
  creates a port and applies port security to it, while letting the platform choose goes down a path
  that never looks at the setting. It is kept as an argument rather than silently ignored, because
  it does apply on the other path.
* **Security groups are not offered.** A router interface is created without any and no endpoint
  adds them afterwards. They belong on the machines behind the router.
* **A static route through an interface pins it.** The platform refuses to detach an interface while
  a route's next hop sits on the network behind it, so a router's routes have to be destroyed before
  its interfaces. Terraform only knows that if the configuration says so -- which route needs which
  interface is a routing decision the API does not report. Put a `depends_on` on every route that
  points through an interface you manage, or a destroy can stop with
  `… cannot be deleted, as it is required by one or more routes`. The same applies to any change
  that *replaces* the interface, such as setting `ip_address` on one that did not have it.
* **Destroying the router takes its interfaces with it.** Terraform's graph already destroys these
  first, so this only shows up for something attached outside Terraform.

## Timeouts

`create` and `delete` each default to 10 minutes. Create does not return until the new port appears
on the router: the attach endpoint answers with the router rather than the port it made, so the port
id -- the only handle detaching has -- is found by watching the router's interface list.

## Import

```shell
# <router-id>:<port-id>. The port id is the `id` of the entry whose `type` is
# "Internal interface" in dtcloud_router_interfaces.
terraform import dtcloud_router_interface.app 3f2a1c9e-77b4-4a01-9d3e-2b6c81f4e5a7:8b41d0c6-5e29-4f77-a0d3-9c2e7b1a4f60
```

`port_security_enabled` is **not** recovered: nothing reports it back, so an import assumes the
default, `true`. If the interface was attached with port security off, say so in the configuration
before importing -- otherwise the value in state is wrong and nothing will tell you.
